ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

candidates.name: Tricuspid Atresia
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of a hypoplastic left ventricle and reduced mitral valve orifice suggests tricuspid atresia.

candidates.name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
contradict_spans: a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle and severe right-sided dilation suggests pulmonary atresia, but the presence of a ventricular septal defect contradicts the intact ventricular septum aspect.

candidates.name: Ebstein's Anomaly
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
severe tricuspid regurgitation
contradict_spans: a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial dilation suggests Ebstein's anomaly, but the hypoplastic left ventricle is not typical.

candidates.name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum
support_spans: severe tricuspid regurgitation
bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
candidates.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects could indicate pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum.
candidates.protected_reason: The complexity of the cardiac defects and the presence of multiple septal defects make this diagnosis a possible consideration.

candidates.name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle

candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is consistent with double outlet right ventricle.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be challenging to diagnose due to the variability in the anatomy of the great vessels and the presence of multiple cardiac defects.
